title: Throw a wrench in space
hook: No air, nothing to push on. Can an astronaut move by throwing a wrench?

doesNotKnow: that momentum conservation applies to the thrown mass and the thrower together

misconception: A rocket needs air to push against, so an astronaut cannot move by throwing.
objective: The learner can explain that with no outside force the thrown mass and the thrower gain equal and opposite momentum, so throwing moves the thrower.

claims.text: With no outside force, total momentum stays the same, so the astronaut and wrench gain equal and opposite momentum and the total stays 0.
claims.source: Conservation of momentum for an isolated system (Newton's third law); any mechanics text, for example OpenStax University Physics Vol. 1, section 9.3.

claims.text: An 80 kg astronaut throwing a 2 kg wrench at 10 m/s gives the wrench 20 kg·m/s, so the astronaut drifts the other way at 20 ÷ 80 = 0.25 m/s.
Speeds are measured in the frame where the astronaut started. A throw speed measured relative to the astronaut would differ by the astronaut's own drift.
claims.source: Stated on stage ('Speeds from the start frame') and in the reveal. For 2 kg at 10 m/s the astronaut drifts 0.25 m/s, 2.5% of the throw speed; the stage takes the speed as the wrench's speed in the start frame.

claims.text: The learner's own throws (mass, speed and the resulting drift) follow m v ÷ 80 for the astronaut, the same formula the stage draws.
claims.source: Reveal quotes the first and last distinct throw from the throws list; drift = m v / 80 rounded to 3 places.

claims.text: You do not need anything to push on, only something to push away: this is how rockets work in space.
claims.source: A rocket expels exhaust mass backwards and gains forward momentum by the same conservation law (no air needed).

claims.text: On the stage the astronaut's move after 1 s is drawn 10 times larger than the wrench's scale so it can be seen; momentum is mass times speed.
claims.source: Drawing scale in Demo.tsx (ASTRO_PX = 45 px per metre against 4.5 px per metre for the wrench); momentum = mass x velocity, standard definition.

recall.question: A 60 kg skater at rest on frictionless ice throws a 3 kg ball forward at 10 m/s. The skater then moves...
recall.why: The ball carries 3 × 10 = 30 kg·m/s, so the skater gets 30 backwards: 30 ÷ 60 = 0.5 m/s.
